bullets.title: Tame July CPI lifts S&P, NASDAQ; VIX hits year-low; September hold priced at 62%
bullets.body: S&P 500 closed +0.27% at 7,749 and NASDAQ +0.50% at 26,579 after July CPI came in benign. Markets now price 62% odds of a September Fed rate hold. VIX fell to its lowest level of the year, with sentiment described as 'all greed, no fear.' Gold jumped above $4,409/oz (+1%) on lower rate-hike bets.

bullets.title: July federal deficit blows out to record $432B, well above $346B estimate
bullets.body: The U.S. July budget deficit came in at $432.3B vs. a $346B consensus estimate and $291B year-ago — the largest monthly deficit in over five years. Medicare, Social Security, and net interest were the largest expenditures; annualized interest expense on public debt now runs $1.37T, on pace to surpass Social Security as the largest federal budget line item.

bullets.title: Treasury yields driven by debt supply weight, not inflation fears — post-CPI action confirms
bullets.body: Despite a benign CPI print and moderating rate-hike expectations, today's Treasury price action supports the thesis that elevated yields reflect structural debt supply pressure rather than inflation or Fed dynamics. Government and corporate issuance are the primary yield drivers.

bullets.title: Market rally supported by $1T+ buybacks, systematic rebalancing, and returning retail — but who buys higher?
bullets.body: The bid underpinning equities reflects $1T+ of corporate buybacks, systematic rebalancing flows, and retail returning to markets. SPY weekly volume is on track for its lowest since Feb 2025, raising the question of who is forced to buy at elevated levels.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade intact; oil near $89/bbl; Brent +0.08%; copper hits record $14k/ton
bullets.body: Diplomatic deadlock on the Strait of Hormuz persists with Iran and the U.S. unable to agree on concessions; Pakistan and Qatar mediating. Brent crude settled at $88.98/bbl with Hormuz traffic sharply reduced. Separately, copper breached $14,000/ton — a record outside January — on U.S. tariff front-running and Chinese demand, while LME settled -0.2% at $14,132/ton with stockpiles falling for 40 consecutive periods. IEA forecasts a 1.8M bpd global oil deficit this quarter.

bullets.title: Goldman: 'Path of least resistance for S&P is higher' but cautions persist
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs strategist Pasquariello characterized the S&P 500's near-term path as higher but flagged macro headwinds that could limit gains. Separately, Goldman agreed to acquire NEOS Investments for up to $2.25B, adding $30B in actively-managed ETF assets.

bullets.title: Cisco Q4 FY26 massive beat: $17.3B revenue +18% YoY; Q1 guide $18.0-18.2B vs $16.84B consensus
bullets.body: Cisco reported Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.22 (vs. $1.17 est.), revenue of $17.3B (+18% YoY, vs. $16.83B est.), and non-GAAP operating margin of 35.9%. Q1 revenue guidance of $18.0-18.2B and EPS of $1.32-1.34 both crushed consensus; FY2027 EPS guided to $5.05-5.11 vs. $4.84 est. Product revenue grew 24% YoY.

bullets.title: Coherent Q4 FY26 beats: $2.05B revenue +34% YoY; Q1 guide midpoint $2.3B above consensus $2.15B
bullets.body: COHR reported Q4 revenue of $2.05B (vs. $1.98B est.), non-GAAP gross margin of 40.2%, and EPS of $1.74 (vs. $1.58 est.) — a 74% YoY increase. Q1 guidance of $2.2-2.4B revenue and $1.85-2.05 EPS both exceed consensus; data center and comms now represent 79% of revenue. Management guided FY27 growth to accelerate vs. FY26.

bullets.title: Coherent moving up stack into OCS/full systems — new competitive threat to Ciena, Cisco, Nokia
bullets.body: Coherent's expansion beyond components into optical coherent subsystems and full systems creates a new competitive dynamic for incumbent optical networking OEMs. The optics segment remains 'lumpy' with scale not yet achieved, but AI infrastructure spend is broadening beyond accelerators into sustained multi-layer investment — a positive read-through from COHR's supplier vantage point.

bullets.title: CoreWeave quarterly demand data lifts AI infrastructure stocks broadly
bullets.body: CoreWeave reported sustained and growing demand for computing power, sparking a rally across AI infrastructure names. Bullish flow in CoreWeave was flagged as among the strongest of the day. Separately, market participant Eric Vishria argued the entire AI ecosystem — CSPs, neoclouds, NVIDIA, chip startups, and large models — is positioned to win.

bullets.title: Michael Burry discloses shorts in NBIS, MU, ORCL and puts on SOXX
bullets.body: Burry's 13F shows he doubled down on his Nebius (NBIS) short and added new short positions in Micron (MU) and Oracle (ORCL), plus put options on the SOXX semiconductor ETF — a broad bearish bet against AI infrastructure beneficiaries even as the group rallied sharply.

bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day Thursday at 9am ET; MSCI ACWI adds SNDK and CART
bullets.body: SanDisk (SNDK) hosts its investor day Thursday morning with new long-term agreements (NBMs) expected to be announced — a potential sector catalyst. Separately, MSCI named SNDK among the three largest additions to the ACWI index by full market cap (55 total additions, 92 deletions), triggering index-fund rebalancing flows.

bullets.title: Robinhood July metrics strong: AUM +19% YoY to $355B, equity volume +59%, options +66%
bullets.body: HOOD's July 2026 metrics showed 28.5M funded customers (+1.77M YoY), $355B total platform assets (+19% YoY), net deposits of $5.6B at 18% annualized growth, equity notional volume of $333B (+59% YoY), and 324M options contracts traded (+66% YoY) — reflecting robust retail engagement in the current market environment.

bullets.title: US-Canada tariff negotiations stalled; companies retaining price hikes despite tariff refunds
bullets.body: Canada and the U.S. are not ready to close a tariff deal with Canada unsatisfied by the latest U.S. offer. Separately, observers note that while tariff refunds are being issued, companies are retaining price increases rather than passing savings to consumers — implying margin expansion at consumer expense rather than demand-stimulating price relief.

bullets.title: Fiscal concerns building: mortgage delinquencies hit decade highs as interest costs surge
bullets.body: 30+ day mortgage delinquencies reached levels not seen in over a decade last quarter. The U.S. government's interest expense hit $1.37T over the trailing 12 months, on pace to surpass Social Security as the largest budget line item. Combined with the record July deficit, fiscal stress indicators are accumulating.

bullets.title: Novo Holdings ($109B fund) resumes full allocation; U.S. renewable energy flagged as compelling
bullets.body: Novo Holdings paused investments earlier in 2024 amid tariff and rate uncertainty but has returned to normal allocation, with the CEO citing improving U.S. market attractiveness. The fund specifically highlighted U.S. renewable energy and infrastructure as materially more attractively valued, driven by surging AI data center electricity demand.

bullets.title: Fed speakers Thursday: Cleveland's Hammack and Richmond's Barkin; near-term data remains gating factor for September hike
bullets.body: Multiple Fed officials (Waller, Williams, Cook, Jefferson, Paulson, Daly) have communicated that supporting data — not just an outlook shift — would be needed to justify a September rate hike. Cleveland Fed President Hammack and Richmond's Barkin speak Thursday morning, with natural gas inventory data at 10:30am ET also on the calendar.

bullets.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro release outperforms Nvidia Nemotron on agentic tasks with fraction of parameters
bullets.body: DeepSeek released V4 Pro 0813 (1.5T parameters), claiming it beats Nemotron3 Ultra on agentic tasks; the Flash variant beats Nemotron with 4.2x fewer active parameters and ~2x fewer total parameters. The release keeps the efficiency-vs-scale debate live and is a read-through for compute demand assumptions underpinning AI infrastructure bulls.

bullets.title: AI spending broadening: agentic AI shifting compute architecture; memory wall emerges as key constraint
bullets.body: Multiple sources highlight that AI infrastructure investment is evolving beyond accelerator procurement into sustained multi-layer spend. AMD flagged agentic AI as reshaping compute requirements. Separately, photonics-background observers argue the memory wall — data movement, not compute — is becoming the primary AI bottleneck, with photonic fabrics and large-scale memory pooling as potential solutions.

bullets.title: Copper near record $14k/ton; aluminum -1.6% on US-Iran ceasefire extension; gold +1% to $4,409
bullets.body: Cross-asset commodity moves: copper at record $14,132/ton (LME -0.2%) driven by tariff front-running and Chinese demand with stockpiles falling for 40 consecutive sessions. Aluminum slumped 1.6% to $3,310.50 after reports of a U.S.-Iran 60-day ceasefire extension. Gold surged 1% to $4,409.35/oz on easing rate-hike fears after benign CPI.
